A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffSampling work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, tables, figures, and qualitative examples can be matched without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v4 reports original decoding experiments on mathematical problem solving, XSum summarization, divergent association, and WritingPrompts, with quantitative results and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations using 70B models and a WritingPrompts unsafe-content assessment.

M1.justification: The three specified procedures—DiffSampling-cut, DiffSampling-lb, and DiffSampling-minp—retain their truncation rules and subsequent temperature scaling. Algorithm 1 is relocated and its variables reformatted; no procedural revision is documented.

E1.justification: v5 removes the additional evaluation on 1,000 examples from the MetaMathQA training corpus reported in v4 Appendix C.1 and Table 6. The four principal task families remain; the larger-model tests and safety assessment reuse existing task data.

E2.justification: WritingPrompts Table 4 drops Top-σ and the additional comparison rows labelled DiffS.-scores and DiffS.-σ. The five principal baselines remain unchanged, including in the new larger-model comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces pretrained and instructed Meta-Llama-3-70B configurations, quantized to 4 bits, across the retained tasks at temperature 1.0. The new safety evaluation uses Llama-Guard-3-8B to assess unsafe-output probabilities across temperatures and temperature placements. Existing principal benchmark settings otherwise remain substantially unchanged; the revised XSum scores do not establish an undocumented protocol change.

E4.justification: v5 adds substantial analysis of whether findings persist with larger models, including repetition and greedy-like behavior, plus an unsafe-content check across decoding settings. Existing temperature-order experiments, threshold ablations, ten-noun DAT evaluation, and qualitative examples are retained. The new trade-off plots largely redisplay existing temperature experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose seeds 1, 42, and 121 and retain the same reporting practices: means and standard errors for specified run-level results, and 95% confidence intervals for output-level metrics. New experiments extend these practices without documenting increased repetitions or new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: XSum results change extensively in Table 3 and corresponding temperature and ablation tables. For instructed DiffSampling-cut, Table 3 changes ROUGE-1 from 0.25 to 0.23 and coherence from 0.69 to 0.63; the PDFs do not explain these revisions. v5 also adds 70B and unsafe-content results, while removing the MetaMathQA evaluation and three WritingPrompts rows.

T1.justification: New Appendix A introduces explicit smoothing-mixture assumptions and two propositions with proofs relating safe truncation to probability gaps and true-support size. v4 provided the discrete-derivative definition and an intuitive argument, without these formal conditions or derivations.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains the same three derivative-based decoding strategies, intended to preserve quality while allowing greater diversity across four task families. The revised abstract and conclusion emphasize sampling from a larger token set, restating the existing rationale without changing the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5.6 explicitly qualifies comparisons involving different temperature placements. Appendix E adds interpretations of model-size-dependent greediness and repetition, while the broader-impact statement distinguishes token-support correctness from content safety. v5 also adds metric-interpretation guidance and practical parameter-selection recommendations.

D1.justification: v5 adds a code/results repository link, documents the new models' 4-bit precision, and expands metric-computation details in Appendix C. The hardware, Python version, seed identities, and principal implementation paragraph are unchanged. Repository availability itself was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v5 adds references to Llama Guard for the safety assessment and Top-H decoding in the future-work discussion. Existing decoding-method positioning remains substantially unchanged; Top-H is not added as an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: v5 makes targeted paragraph revisions, expands explanations, changes author-information formatting, and reorganizes the appendices, including moving the temperature-position study into the temperature appendix. Most existing narrative and qualitative-example text is retained, rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v5 adds dedicated safety and larger-model tables, a larger-model DAT figure, and three multi-panel quality-diversity plots. Figure 3 is redrawn to distinguish temperature placement, Table 4 loses three rows, and the MetaMathQA table disappears. Algorithm and appendix-display placement also change substantially; most original figures and qualitative tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 improves transparency through explicit assumptions, clearer temperature comparisons, expanded metric documentation, and a code/results link. The larger-model and safety checks provide useful additional evidence. However, some new interpretations overstate that evidence: Appendix E describes mathematical accuracy as on par or better than greedy, while Table 7 reports 21.27 versus 22.56 for instructed 70B MATH. Together with unexplained XSum revisions, this limits the overall gain.
